EPJ (Elektronisk Patient Journal) is a clinical journal system used in Danish hospitals to record and manage patient data. In the context of national healthcare quality monitoring, the EPJ serves as the primary reference standard for the local validation of the [[akut-kirurgi-databasen|Akut Kirurgi Databasen]] (AKDB), a national quality database tracking acute high-risk abdominal surgery [^src1]. 

The primary significance of the EPJ in this workflow is to ensure that the patient population and clinical details captured by the national database accurately reflect the actual clinical reality [^src1]. When hospitals and regions validate their data, they compare their local clinical registrations in the EPJ against the data reported to the Landspatientregisteret (LPR) and subsequently transferred to the AKDB via KKA deliveries in the LIS systems [^src1]. Specifically, the EPJ is used as the ground truth to verify the total number of patients, confirm patient identities, check the correctness of operation dates, and ensure that other clinical variables are complete and accurate [^src1]. 

This validation process is a critical component of the practical quality improvement work conducted across regions and hospitals [^src1]. By using the EPJ to identify missing or incorrect entries, data managers can perform necessary retroactive registrations, thereby maintaining the integrity of the national database and supporting the broader quality development strategy managed by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) [^src1].
